correctness.rationale: PASS: Every random variable and quantifier is explicit. Pairwise exponential comparisons give a uniform O(n^{-1}) obstruction bound for non-neighboring inversions. The exact run-order race identity and independence of separated clock sets bound all mixed event probabilities. A uniformly dominated inclusion–exclusion expansion proves convergence of the full spatial Laplace functional to the inhomogeneous Poisson process. The rank permutation is determined by its inversion set, so on the high-probability event its only changes are disjoint adjacent transpositions. Inversion-count and parity limits follow, including zero intensity. The exact geometric identity follows from sequential race probabilities; a disjoint-comparison bound settles the nr_n→infinity case. The actual standalone exact checker passed 340 assertions over sizes 2–7; it is corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: PASS with residual priority risk: Comparison against full text of Turvey (arXiv:2610.11895v1), the earlier Babson et al. full paper (arXiv:2407.20226), and Guiver–Snelson’s Plackett–Luce likelihood paper separates finite order-law geometry and ranking inference from spatial rare-inversion asymptotics. Scientific-record searches on equivalent exponential-race rankings, adjacency errors, Gumbel recovery, and spatial Poisson limits returned no directly covering claim; named related records address a three-score feasible-order polytope, heterogeneous order-statistic identifiability, proportional-hazard marginals, or a different MIMO Poisson–Gumbel mechanism. A 2000 independent-utility inequality paper had only abstract access; an unindexed or broadly formulated prior theorem could still dominate this result. value.rationale: PASS: Ranking recovery under strongly separated strengths is a natural, interpretable probabilistic question in exponential races and random-utility orders. The theorem yields a full spatial error process and, on an event whose failure is uniformly O(1/n), the entire permutation structure; this is stronger information than a scalar Poisson approximation. It identifies the exact order-recovery threshold and a Gumbel crossover in the geometric-rate family and accommodates nonconstant spatial error intensities. The object and exact invariants are motivated by reliability of a ranking, not by an arbitrary slice or a tiny numerical improvement. No extension to nonexponential laws is claimed.
